data.body:
Implementation landed for review as Gerrit change 1602 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1602).

Patch set 1 passed LLM-Review +1 but took Verified -1 from tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py: that guard sources every MCP tool mechanically from list_tools() and fails any new one not classified as CANONICAL / EXEMPT_GENERIC / NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT. It lives under tests/interfaces/, so the plan's AC6 verify command (pytest tests/unit -k mcp) could not have caught it.

Resolution, and a correction to the plan: the plan argued that src/rebar/schemas/ was NOT needed because check_mcp_models.MODEL_SCHEMAS is opt-in. That was wrong — the coverage guard's classification is not opt-in. Since the tool returns a genuinely structured {ok, verdict, reason, verified_at_sha, signed_at} shape rather than a string ack, the honest classification is CANONICAL, which requires a real canonical schema. Added src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_status.schema.json plus the PLAN_REVIEW_STATUS constant and OUTPUT_SCHEMAS entry (the every-schema-file-is-wired guard requires wiring), keyed by MCP tool name like grounding_info because the CLI reaches this read through 'review-plan --status' rather than its own subcommand. The ticket's original Scope line naming src/rebar/schemas/ was therefore right; file_impact now records all eight paths.

Second deviation: adding a nested tool pushed register_read_tools past its FROZEN McCabe ceiling (31 -> 32) in the shrink-only complexity baseline. Rather than raise a locked baseline, the tool is registered from a small module-level _register_plan_review_tools, following the seam register_bridge_tools already established in the same file.

Local gates green: ruff, mypy, MCP model schema drift, gen_mcp_reference.py --check, tests/unit -k mcp (48 passed), and the full tests/interfaces suite (1760 passed, 12 skipped) including live validation of the tool's real output against the new schema.
